note: Review-only file, not a TestsData row. Numeric keys should receive a final manual check before production insertion.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of engineering drawing?

options.label: A
options.text: Communicate technical shape, size and details in a standard visual form

options.label: C
options.text: Replace all physical measurements with colour

options.label: D
options.text: Record only the cost of a component

questions.rationale: Engineering drawing communicates technical geometry and specifications.

questions.text: Which line type conventionally represents visible object outlines?
questions.rationale: Visible edges use continuous thick object lines.

questions.text: Which line type commonly represents hidden edges?
questions.rationale: Hidden detail is represented by dashed lines.

questions.text: Which line is commonly used to indicate a centre or axis?
questions.rationale: Centre lines are commonly thin chain lines.

questions.text: What is the role of a dimension line?

options.label: A
options.text: Show the extent and value of a measured feature

options.label: D
options.text: Separate the title from the sheet

questions.rationale: Dimension lines carry the measured extent between extension lines.

questions.text: What is the Representative Fraction (RF) of a scale?

options.label: A
options.text: Drawing length divided by actual length in the same units

options.label: B
options.text: Actual length divided by drawing length in different units

options.label: C
options.text: Drawing area divided by actual area

questions.rationale: RF is drawing length divided by actual length using consistent units.

questions.text: A drawing is full-size. What is its RF?
questions.rationale: Full size represents the object with equal drawing and actual lengths.

questions.text: Which view typically shows width and height?
questions.rationale: The front elevation shows front-facing dimensions such as width and height.

questions.text: Which view typically shows width and depth?
questions.rationale: The plan shows the object's footprint, including width and depth.

questions.text: What is an isometric drawing used to communicate?

options.label: A
options.text: A pictorial view showing three principal directions in one view

options.label: D
options.text: A list of dimensions without geometry

questions.rationale: An isometric view provides a 3D pictorial representation.

questions.text: Which curve is defined by points equidistant from a focus and a directrix?
questions.rationale: A parabola has equal distances to its focus and directrix.

questions.text: Which curve is a closed conic with two foci?
questions.rationale: An ellipse is a closed conic with two foci.

questions.text: Which conic has two separate branches?
questions.rationale: A hyperbola has two branches.

questions.text: Which ellipse construction method uses two circles with a common centre but different radii?
questions.rationale: The concentric-circle method uses circles sharing a centre.

questions.text: Which curve is traced by a point on a circle rolling along a straight line without slipping?
questions.rationale: A cycloid is generated by a point on a rolling circle.

questions.text: A circle rolls outside another fixed circle. The path of a point on the rolling circle is which curve?
questions.rationale: An epicycloid is generated by rolling externally on a fixed circle.

questions.text: A circle rolls inside a fixed circle. The path of a point on the rolling circle is which curve?
questions.rationale: A hypocycloid is generated by rolling inside a fixed circle.

questions.text: Which curve is traced by the free end of a taut string as it is unwound from a base curve?
questions.rationale: An involute is traced by a taut unwinding string end.

questions.text: What is a tangent to a curve at a point?

options.label: A
options.text: A line that gives the curve's local direction at that point

options.label: B
options.text: A line always parallel to the drawing border

options.label: C
options.text: A line showing the hidden part only

questions.rationale: A tangent represents the curve's instantaneous direction at the contact point.

questions.text: What is the normal at a point on a curve?

options.label: A
options.text: A line perpendicular to the tangent at that point

options.label: B
options.text: A line parallel to the tangent

questions.rationale: The normal is perpendicular to the tangent.

questions.text: In first-angle projection, where is the plan placed relative to the front elevation?

options.label: D
options.text: To the left of the sheet only

questions.rationale: The top view is unfolded below the front view in first-angle projection.

questions.text: In third-angle projection, where is the plan placed relative to the front elevation?
questions.rationale: Third-angle places the plan above the front elevation.

questions.text: Which group contains the three principal orthographic views?

options.label: C
options.text: Plan, section and colour key only

questions.rationale: Front, top and side views are the principal orthographic views.

questions.text: A line is parallel to a reference plane. What does its projection on that plane show ideally?
questions.rationale: A line parallel to a plane projects at true length.

questions.text: A plane surface is parallel to a principal projection plane. What does its view on that plane show?
questions.rationale: A parallel plane projects without foreshortening.

questions.text: What is a sectional view primarily used to show?

options.label: A
options.text: Internal features exposed by an imaginary cutting plane

questions.rationale: Sectional views reveal internal details.

questions.text: What is an auxiliary plane useful for in projection problems?

options.label: A
options.text: Showing true shape or length when a feature is inclined to principal planes

questions.rationale: Auxiliary projection can reveal true geometry of inclined features.

questions.text: What does a drawing scale of 1:5 indicate?

options.label: A
options.text: One unit on the drawing represents five units on the object

options.label: B
options.text: Five units on the drawing represent one on the object

options.label: C
options.text: The drawing is enlarged five times

questions.rationale: RF 1:5 is a reduction scale.

questions.text: Which instrument is commonly used to draw accurate circles and arcs?
questions.rationale: A compass draws circles and arcs.

questions.text: What does BIS refer to in standards-based drawing practice in India?
questions.rationale: BIS is the Bureau of Indian Standards.

questions.text: Which type of scale represents a drawing smaller than the actual object?
questions.rationale: A reducing scale has RF less than 1.

questions.text: Which type of scale represents an object larger than its actual size?
questions.rationale: An enlarging scale has RF greater than 1.

questions.text: A drawing length is 20 mm for an actual length of 100 mm. What is the RF?
Which view is most appropriate for showing the top footprint of a rectangular block?
questions.rationale: The plan shows the top-view footprint.

questions.text: Which practice helps make dimensions readable?

options.label: A
options.text: Use consistent dimension/extension lines with clear values

options.label: B
options.text: Place dimension text randomly over the object

options.label: C
options.text: Use hidden lines as all dimensions

questions.rationale: Consistent dimensioning supports interpretation.

questions.text: Which line represents the boundary between a visible surface and empty space?
questions.rationale: Visible edges use continuous thick object lines.

questions.text: In an isometric view, the three principal axes are conventionally separated by what angle in the drawing plane?
questions.rationale: Isometric axes are 120° apart.

questions.text: Which statement about an isometric scale is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: It produces foreshortened isometric lengths compared with true lengths

options.label: B
options.text: It converts every circle into a straight line

options.label: C
options.text: It is always the same as RF

questions.rationale: Isometric projection uses reduced lengths along isometric axes.

questions.text: Which conic construction method is specifically listed for ellipse construction?
questions.rationale: The syllabus includes the oblong method for ellipse construction.

questions.text: Which curve family has constructions involving tangent and normal?
questions.rationale: Cycloidal curves are constructed with tangents and normals in the syllabus.

questions.text: A component is 150 mm long. At RF 1:5, how long should it be drawn?
questions.rationale: Drawing length=150×1/5=30 mm.

questions.text: A drawing measures 60 mm for an actual length of 30 mm. Which scale is used?
questions.rationale: RF=60/30=2, so the scale is 2:1.

questions.text: A line has true length 80 mm and is parallel to VP. Which projection shows its true length?
questions.rationale: A line parallel to VP appears at true length in elevation.

questions.text: A plane lamina is inclined to HP but parallel to VP. Which view shows true shape?

options.label: C
options.text: A side view in every case

questions.rationale: A surface parallel to VP is shown in true shape in elevation.

questions.text: A point lies above HP and in front of VP. Which quadrant is it in?
questions.rationale: Above HP and in front of VP defines the first quadrant.

questions.text: Which principle distinguishes first-angle from third-angle projection?

options.label: A
options.text: Relative placement of object, observer and projection plane

questions.rationale: The methods differ in the relative object/observer/plane positions.

questions.text: Under first-angle projection, where is the right-side view placed relative to the front view?
questions.rationale: The right-side view appears left of the front view in first-angle projection.

questions.text: Under third-angle projection, where is the right-side view placed?
questions.rationale: Third-angle places the right-side view to the right.

questions.text: A physical length of 2.4 m is represented by 120 mm. What is the RF?
A conic needs to be constructed from focus/directrix information. Which construction family is relevant?
questions.rationale: Focus/directrix definitions guide conic construction.

questions.text: A drawing length is 75 mm at RF 3:2. What is the actual length?
questions.rationale: Actual length=75÷1.5=50 mm.

questions.text: A road section is 4.5 km and must fit as 90 mm on a drawing. What RF is required?
A point has zero height above HP and lies in front of VP. Where does it lie?

options.label: A
options.text: On HP and in front of VP

options.label: D
options.text: Above HP and in front of VP

questions.rationale: Zero height places the point on HP.

questions.text: A line is inclined to HP but parallel to VP. Which view gives its true length and inclination to HP?
questions.rationale: Because the line is parallel to VP, the front view gives true length and inclination to HP.

questions.text: A polygon is parallel to HP. Which view shows its true shape?
questions.rationale: A surface parallel to HP shows true shape in plan.

questions.text: A cutting plane passes through a hollow block to reveal its cavity. Which view shows the internal arrangement?
questions.rationale: A section reveals internal features.

questions.text: An ellipse construction uses two concentric circles. What is the key feature?

options.label: A
options.text: Corresponding radial divisions and projected points locate points on the ellipse

options.label: C
options.text: The method only constructs a cycloid

options.label: D
options.text: The method turns all lines into hidden lines

questions.rationale: Corresponding divisions of concentric circles locate ellipse points.

questions.text: A cycloid is constructed from a rolling circle. What motion generates it?

options.label: A
options.text: A point on the circle rolling without slipping along a straight line

options.label: B
options.text: A point rotating about a fixed centre only

options.label: C
options.text: A line parallel to the directrix

options.label: D
options.text: A cone cut by a plane

questions.rationale: Rolling along a straight line generates a cycloid.

questions.text: A circle rolls around the outside of a fixed circle. Which curve fits?
questions.rationale: External rolling generates an epicycloid.

questions.text: For a circle, where is the normal at a point located?

options.label: A
options.text: Along the radius through the point of contact

options.label: B
options.text: Along the tangent through the point

questions.rationale: The radius at the contact point is perpendicular to the tangent.

questions.text: An object is 125 mm long and drawn at RF 4:1. What drawing length is required?
questions.rationale: An enlarging scale multiplies the actual length by 4: 500 mm.

questions.text: A scale is RF 1:25. A measured feature is 84 mm on the drawing. What is its actual length?
questions.rationale: Actual length=84×25=2,100 mm.

questions.text: A line is inclined to both HP and VP. How should its true length be found from projections?

options.label: A
options.text: Use projection construction/auxiliary views or successive rotations as required

options.label: B
options.text: Assume either projection equals true length

options.label: C
options.text: Take the shorter projection as true length

options.label: D
options.text: Replace both projections by an isometric scale

questions.rationale: A line inclined to both principal planes is foreshortened in both views.

questions.text: A plane is inclined to HP and its true shape is needed. Which method is appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: Use an auxiliary plane/view parallel to the lamina or a change-of-plane method

options.label: D
options.text: Replace its boundary with a centre line

questions.rationale: An auxiliary view parallel to the surface reveals its true shape.

questions.text: A point is above HP and behind VP. Which quadrant is it in?
questions.rationale: Above HP and behind VP identifies the second quadrant.

questions.text: A point is below HP and in front of VP. Which quadrant is it in?
questions.rationale: Below HP and in front of VP identifies the fourth quadrant.

questions.text: Why should orthographic views be aligned consistently?

options.label: A
options.text: Corresponding edges and dimensions can be related across views

options.label: D
options.text: It converts orthographic projection into perspective

questions.rationale: Alignment links corresponding dimensions and edges.

questions.text: A sectioned drawing uses hatching on cut material. What does the hatching indicate?

options.label: A
options.text: Material intersected by the cutting plane

questions.rationale: Section lines identify the cut material.

questions.text: An isometric drawing uses true lengths along its axes. How does this differ from isometric projection?

options.label: A
options.text: Isometric drawing generally uses true lengths; isometric projection uses foreshortened lengths

options.label: B
options.text: Isometric projection always uses perspective convergence

options.label: D
options.text: An isometric drawing cannot show three dimensions

questions.rationale: The conventional distinction is true versus foreshortened isometric lengths.

questions.text: A tangent and normal are needed at a plotted point. What relationship must hold?

options.label: A
options.text: They are perpendicular at that point

options.label: C
options.text: They meet only at a focus

questions.rationale: The normal is perpendicular to the tangent.

questions.text: A drawing length is 42 mm and actual length is 3.5 m. Which RF is correct?
A design uses RF 5:1. An object edge is 18 mm long. How long should it appear on the drawing?
questions.rationale: Drawing length=5×18=90 mm.

questions.text: A line's front and top projections are both shorter than its true length. What does this suggest?

options.label: A
options.text: The line is inclined to both HP and VP

options.label: B
options.text: It is parallel to both HP and VP

options.label: C
options.text: It lies on both principal planes

questions.rationale: Inclination to both planes generally foreshortens both projections.

questions.text: Which arrangement is characteristic of third-angle projection?

options.label: A
options.text: Plan above front view, right-side view to the right

options.label: B
options.text: Plan below front view, right-side view left

options.label: D
options.text: Plan below title block regardless of elevation

questions.rationale: Third-angle places plan above and the right-side view to the right.

questions.text: Which methods are suitable for constructing a parabola under the syllabus?

options.label: A
options.text: Rectangle method or method of tangents (triangle method)

questions.rationale: Both rectangle and tangent/triangle methods are listed for parabolas.

questions.text: A hyperbola is constructed from focus and directrix information. Which method family applies?
questions.rationale: The syllabus includes directrix-focus methods for conics.

questions.text: A cycloidal curve's tangent is required. What should be prepared first?

options.label: A
options.text: Accurate curve-generation points and rolling-circle geometry

questions.rationale: Tangent construction depends on correctly locating the curve.

questions.text: A long object must be represented smaller while actual length remains clear. What information is important?

options.label: A
options.text: Appropriate RF, clear dimensioning and scale notation

options.label: C
options.text: Omit dimensions because a scale exists

questions.rationale: Scale and dimensions help readers interpret a reduced drawing.

questions.text: A circular plane is inclined to HP. Why can its top view appear elliptical?

options.label: A
options.text: Projection foreshortens dimensions when the circle is inclined to the projection plane

options.label: C
options.text: All circles always draw as ellipses

options.label: D
options.text: The scale ratio changes non-uniformly in every view

questions.rationale: An inclined circle projects as a foreshortened ellipse.

questions.text: A student uses hidden lines for every visible edge. What is the correction?

options.label: A
options.text: Use continuous thick object lines for visible edges and dashed lines for hidden edges

questions.rationale: Line conventions distinguish visible from hidden geometry.

questions.text: A 3.6 m component is drawn at RF 1:40. Does its 90 mm drawing length fit a target sheet length of 90 mm?

options.label: B
options.text: No, because it should be 9 mm

options.label: C
options.text: No, because it should be 144 mm

questions.text: A point is 20 mm above HP and 30 mm behind VP. Which quadrant and general view placement apply?

options.label: A
options.text: First quadrant; elevation above XY and plan below XY

options.label: B
options.text: Second quadrant; both projections above XY

options.label: C
options.text: Third quadrant; both projections below XY

options.label: D
options.text: Fourth quadrant; elevation above and plan below

questions.rationale: Above HP and behind VP is second quadrant; both projections lie above XY.

questions.text: A line of true length 100 mm is parallel to VP and inclined 30° to HP. Which describes the front view?

options.label: A
options.text: 100 mm long and inclined 30° to XY

options.label: B
options.text: 50 mm long because every projection is half

options.label: C
options.text: 86.6 mm long because it is parallel to VP

options.label: D
options.text: 0 mm because it is inclined to HP

questions.rationale: Parallelism to VP preserves true length in elevation.

questions.text: A circular lamina is inclined to HP but parallel to VP. Which view shows its true shape and why?

options.label: A
options.text: Front view, because the lamina is parallel to VP

options.label: B
options.text: Top view, because every plane appears true in plan

options.label: D
options.text: Isometric view because it never foreshortens

questions.rationale: A plane parallel to VP shows true shape in elevation.

questions.text: A 240 mm shaft is represented at RF 3:5. A second sheet enlarges the first drawing 2:1. What is the second drawing length?
questions.rationale: First drawing=240×3/5=144 mm; doubled gives 288 mm.

questions.text: A cavity is not visible externally and its internal layout must be shown. Which view is best?

options.label: A
options.text: An appropriate sectional view with conventional section lining

options.label: B
options.text: Only a top view with no section indication

options.label: C
options.text: A hidden line for every interior surface regardless of view

questions.rationale: A section reveals internal detail.

questions.text: A circle rolls externally around a fixed circle, and a point on its circumference is traced. Which curve results?
questions.rationale: External rolling generates an epicycloid.

questions.text: A surface is inclined to both principal planes and neither principal view shows true shape. What construction strategy is defensible?

options.label: A
options.text: Construct an auxiliary view parallel to the surface or use a change-of-plane method

options.label: B
options.text: Assume the shorter view is the true shape

options.label: D
options.text: Replace the boundary with hidden lines

questions.rationale: A view parallel to the surface avoids foreshortening.

questions.text: A drawing length is 72 mm at RF 3:2. The actual component is reduced to one-third of its original length. What is the drawing length of the shorter component at the same RF?
questions.rationale: Original actual=72÷1.5=48 mm; one-third=16 mm; drawing length=16×1.5=24 mm.

questions.text: At a curve point P the tangent is known. What yields the normal at P?

options.label: A
options.text: A line perpendicular to the tangent through P

options.label: B
options.text: A line parallel to the tangent through P

options.label: C
options.text: A line through the focus only

questions.rationale: The normal is perpendicular to the tangent.

questions.text: An object is 2.4 m long at RF 1:25. A detail view enlarges the main drawing 4:1. What is the detail length?
questions.rationale: Main view=2400/25=96 mm; 4× enlargement=384 mm.

questions.text: A 90 mm drawing represents an actual 1.5 m length. A revised actual length is 2.4 m at the same RF. What drawing length is required?
A point lies below HP and behind VP. Which quadrant/view placement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Third quadrant; elevation below XY and plan above XY

options.label: C
options.text: First quadrant; elevation above and plan below

questions.rationale: Below HP and behind VP defines the third quadrant.

questions.text: A line is parallel to HP and inclined to VP. Which projection shows true length?
questions.rationale: A line parallel to HP is true length in plan.

questions.text: A closed conic has a constant sum of distances from any point on it to two fixed foci. Which curve is it?
questions.rationale: An ellipse has a constant sum of focal distances.

questions.text: A drawing shows equal foreshortening along three principal axes. Which projection is intended?
questions.rationale: Isometric projection equally foreshortens its principal axes.

questions.text: A designer has top/front views and needs a pictorial view. Which conversion is called for?
questions.rationale: The syllabus covers converting orthographic views into isometric views.

questions.text: A plane polygon appears edge-on in an orthographic view. What does that indicate?

options.label: A
options.text: Its plane is perpendicular to that projection plane

options.label: B
options.text: Its plane is parallel to that projection plane

options.label: C
options.text: The view must be true shape

questions.rationale: A plane perpendicular to the projection plane projects edge-on.

questions.text: A scale is RF 2:1 and a drawn line measures 35 mm. What is the actual length?
questions.rationale: Actual length=35/2=17.5 mm.

questions.text: A feature's width differs between aligned front and top views. What should be checked first?

options.label: A
options.text: Projection alignment, view orientation and whether the same feature is being compared

options.label: C
options.text: Pencil type for the title only

options.label: D
options.text: Whether the object has a domain name

questions.rationale: Corresponding dimensions should align between correctly arranged views.

questions.text: A 4.8 m object is drawn at RF 1:60. A detail enlarges the main drawing 5:1. What is its detail length?
questions.rationale: Main drawing=4800/60=80 mm; 5× detail=400 mm.

questions.text: A plane inclined to both HP and VP appears foreshortened in both principal views. What is needed for true shape?

options.label: A
options.text: An auxiliary view parallel to the plane or equivalent change-of-plane method

questions.rationale: A view parallel to the plane shows its true shape.

questions.text: In first-angle projection the right-side view appears on the right of the front view. What mistake should be checked?

options.label: A
options.text: The view placement may follow third-angle rather than first-angle convention

questions.rationale: First-angle places the right-side view to the left of the front view.

questions.text: A 180 mm line is drawn at RF 2:3, then the drawing is enlarged by 150%. What is the new length?
questions.rationale: First drawing=180×2/3=120 mm; 150% of 120 mm is 180 mm.

questions.text: A tangent is drawn to a circle at P. What relation should the normal satisfy?

options.label: A
options.text: It passes through the circle's centre and P, perpendicular to the tangent

options.label: B
options.text: It is parallel to the tangent and avoids the centre

options.label: C
options.text: It is a chord not passing through P

questions.rationale: The radius to P is the normal and is perpendicular to the tangent.

questions.text: A drawing uses continuous thick lines for hidden and visible edges alike. What is the main problem?

options.label: A
options.text: The reader cannot distinguish visible outlines from concealed edges

questions.rationale: Line types distinguish visible from hidden geometry.

questions.text: A circle rolls internally along the inside of a fixed circle. Which curve family results?
questions.rationale: Internal rolling generates a hypocycloid.

questions.text: A line of 52 mm on the drawing represents 1.3 m. Which RF and scale type apply?
Both principal projections of a line are foreshortened. How should its true length be found?

options.label: A
options.text: Use projection geometry/auxiliary view rather than assuming either projection is true length

options.label: B
options.text: Choose the shorter view as true length

questions.rationale: An oblique line is generally foreshortened in both principal views.

questions.text: A parabola is constructed by the focus-directrix method. Which condition defines its points?

options.label: A
options.text: Distance to focus equals perpendicular distance to directrix

options.label: B
options.text: Distance to two foci has constant sum

options.label: C
options.text: Points lie on two concentric circles only

options.label: D
options.text: A circle rolls outside another circle

questions.rationale: Equal focus and directrix distances define a parabola.

questions.text: A 5.4 m span must occupy 135 mm on a sheet. What length represents a 7.2 m span at the same RF?
A 120 mm line is parallel to VP and inclined 35° to HP. Which values describe elevation length and inclination?
questions.rationale: Parallel to VP preserves true length in elevation.

questions.text: A line is parallel to HP but inclined 40° to VP. What remains true in plan?

options.label: A
options.text: Its true length and inclination to VP

questions.rationale: A line parallel to HP appears at true length in plan.

questions.text: A plane is parallel to VP but inclined to HP. What does its elevation show?
questions.rationale: Parallelism to VP preserves true shape in elevation.

questions.text: How does an isometric drawing conventionally differ from isometric projection?

options.label: A
options.text: An isometric drawing generally uses true lengths; isometric projection uses foreshortened lengths

options.label: C
options.text: Both must use 1:1 on every diagonal

questions.rationale: The distinction is true lengths versus reduced isometric lengths.

questions.text: In third-angle projection, where is the top view placed relative to the front view?
questions.rationale: Third-angle places the plan above the front view.

questions.text: Two construction methods are used for the same ellipse with unchanged dimensions. What should remain unchanged?

options.label: A
options.text: The target ellipse geometry, although the construction steps differ

options.label: B
options.text: The ellipse necessarily becomes a different conic

questions.rationale: Construction methods are alternatives for locating points on the same ellipse.

questions.text: A scale is RF 1:75. An actual length of 6 m is represented, then the drawing is doubled for a detail. What is the final detail length?
questions.rationale: At 1:75, 6000/75=80 mm; doubling yields 160 mm.

questions.text: An orthographic drawing has aligned views but lacks dimensions and scale notation. What is the principal issue?

options.label: A
options.text: Actual sizes may not be determined reliably

questions.rationale: Dimensions and scale help communicate actual size.

questions.text: A hollow component needs internal detail while retaining the outside geometry. What representation best fits?

options.label: A
options.text: A correctly indicated sectional view with hatching

questions.rationale: A section reveals internal details and maintains external outlines.
